Core rules (they hold for every script):
- **Write runnable JavaScript — NO type syntax.** The script executes as plain JS in a V8 isolate; the TypeScript types are the tool *surface* you read from `get_schema`, not something you write in the body. A type annotation in the code — `: Type`, `as`, `interface`/`type`/`enum`, or generics `<T>` — is a parse error that fails the WHOLE run (zero spend, before any tool call). Author against the types; emit only the JS.
- **One I/O primitive:** `const r = await callTool(name, params)` → `{ ok: true, data, credits_used? } | { ok: false, status, errorType, message }`. `credits_used` is the server's exact charge for that call (data-API tools only; `0` = free/preview, and an async batch SUBMIT — billed at job completion, not on submit) — sum it to track spend mid-run. `upstream_request_id` is the API's own id for that call, present on success and failure alike when the response carried one — quote it when reporting a failed or disputed charge, it is the join key to the API's own record. A failure that stopped for want of credits also carries `top_up_url`, and the run's result then carries `out_of_credits` with the sentence to relay; put that link in your reply exactly as written, since the person who can buy credits is the one reading it. A `permission_error` because the account hasn't completed its first purchase carries `paywall_url` instead — relay that link exactly as written too.
- **await ONLY `callTool`, `sleep`, `paginate`, and `parallelMap`** — the query-builder and result-shaper helpers are synchronous; awaiting one is a harmless no-op (`await` on a non-promise returns it unchanged), just needless — so don't.
- **Fan out INDEPENDENT work — don't await in a loop.** When you have N independent calls (enrich/lookup a list, per-entity sub-queries, several unrelated searches), run them at once with `await parallelMap(items, fn)` instead of a `for … await` loop — far faster and it keeps a big bulk run under the wall-clock (same credits either way). BATCH first (`chunk` to the per-call cap, e.g. 25 for enrich), then `parallelMap` the batches. NEVER parallelize: cursor pagination (use `paginate` — each page needs the prior cursor), dependent steps (`search → enrich`: keep the pipeline sequential, parallelize only WITHIN a stage), or accumulate-then-decide / early-exit (parallel can't stop early → pays for all N).
- **Always branch on `r.ok`** — a failed call does NOT abort the script, so an unchecked failure silently proceeds on empty data and looks like "no results". Use `unwrap(await callTool(...))` when a step must succeed; `execute` also returns a `tool_errors` list, so empty ≠ failed stays visible.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)

3	The file ledger (`ledger/<assessment>/…`, see ARCHITECTURE §5) stays the write path the coordinator, fixers and dashboard
4	already use. Every write is mirrored here, into one SQLite file, so an assessment can be queried with SQL, copied as a
5	single artifact, served behind an API with access control, or rebuilt from the files with `preflight db sync`.
6	
7	Path: `$PREFLIGHT_DB`, default `ledger/preflight.sqlite`. WAL mode, so the coordinator, parallel replay threads and the
8	approve/regress CLIs can write concurrently. Mirroring never raises: a store problem is logged, the file ledger is still
9	authoritative, and `db sync` rebuilds the table rows from the files.
10	"""
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	import json, os, pathlib, sqlite3, sys, threading, time
13	from typing import Any, Iterable
14	
15	from . import config
16	
17	_LOCK = threading.Lock()
18	_INITED: set[str] = set()

22	  assessment_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, state TEXT, mode TEXT, kind TEXT, label TEXT, target_dir TEXT, target_commit TEXT,
23	  started_at TEXT, updated_at REAL, preflight_llm_usd REAL, manifest JSON);

"""SQLite ledger store.

The file ledger (`ledger/<assessment>/…`, see ARCHITECTURE §5) stays the write path the coordinator, fixers and dashboard
already use. Every write is mirrored here, into one SQLite file, so an assessment can be queried with SQL, copied as a
single artifact, served behind an API with access control, or rebuilt from the files with `preflight db sync`.

Path: `$PREFLIGHT_DB`, default `ledger/preflight.sqlite`. WAL mode, so the coordinator, parallel replay threads and the
approve/regress CLIs can write concurrently. Mirroring never raises: a store problem is logged, the file ledger is still
authoritative, and `db sync` rebuilds the table rows from the files.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import json, os, pathlib, sqlite3, sys, threading, time
from typing import Any, Iterable

from . import config

_LOCK = threading.Lock()
_INITED: set[str] = set()

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS assessments (
  assessment_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, state TEXT, mode TEXT, kind TEXT, label TEXT, target_dir TEXT, target_commit TEXT,
  started_at TEXT, updated_at REAL, preflight_llm_usd REAL, manifest JSON);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS runs (
  run_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, assessment_id TEXT NOT NULL, attack_id TEXT, seed_id TEXT, kind TEXT, failed INTEGER, error TEXT,
  target_commit TEXT, mode TEXT, started_at TEXT, duration_ms INTEGER, steps INTEGER, tokens_in INTEGER, tokens_out INTEGER,
  usd REAL, neatlogs_trace_id TEXT, neatlogs_url TEXT, reply TEXT, tool_calls JSON, record JSON);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS runs_assessment ON runs(assessment_id, kind, attack_id);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS verdicts (
  run_id TEXT NOT NULL, grader TEXT NOT NULL, passed INTEGER, violation_step INTEGER, evidence JSON,
  PRIMARY KEY (run_id, grader));
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS steps (
  run_id TEXT NOT NULL, i INTEGER NOT NULL, component TEXT, type TEXT, tool TEXT, result_kind TEXT, tokens INTEGER, usd REAL,
  duration_ms INTEGER, step JSON, PRIMARY KEY (run_id, i));
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clusters (
  assessment_id TEXT NOT NULL, cluster_id TEXT NOT NULL, signature TEXT, family TEXT, status TEXT, attack_ids JSON, run_ids JSON,
  failing_graders JSON, hypothesis TEXT, divergence JSON, record JSON, PRIMARY KEY (assessment_id, cluster_id));
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS attempts (
  assessment_id TEXT NOT NULL, cluster_id TEXT NOT NULL, n INTEGER NOT NULL, author TEXT, backend TEXT, branch TEXT, commit_sha TEXT,
  entire_checkpoint_id TEXT, tests_green INTEGER, status TEXT, cost_usd REAL, replay_before TEXT, replay_after TEXT, summary TEXT,
  record JSON, PRIMARY KEY (assessment_id, cluster_id, n));
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
  assessment_id TEXT NOT NULL, seq INTEGER NOT NULL, ts REAL, type TEXT, cluster_id TEXT, run_id TEXT, payload JSON,
  PRIMARY KEY (assessment_id, seq));
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS events_type ON events(assessment_id, type);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS regressions (
  assessment_id TEXT NOT NULL, cluster_id TEXT NOT NULL, passed INTEGER, blame JSON, record JSON,
  PRIMARY KEY (assessment_id, cluster_id));
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS scorecard AS
  SELECT assessment_id, kind, attack_id, COUNT(*) AS runs, SUM(failed) AS attack_succeeded, ROUND(SUM(usd), 5) AS usd
  FROM runs GROUP BY assessment_id, kind, attack_id;
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS fixes AS
  SELECT a.assessment_id, a.cluster_id, c.family, c.status AS cluster_status, a.n, a.author, a.status, a.tests_green,
         a.replay_before, a.replay_after, a.commit_sha, a.entire_checkpoint_id, a.cost_usd
  FROM attempts a LEFT JOIN clusters c ON c.assessment_id = a.assessment_id AND c.cluster_id = a.cluster_id;
"""


def path() -> pathlib.Path:
    p = os.getenv("PREFLIGHT_DB")
    return pathlib.Path(p) if p else config.LEDGER_DIR / "preflight.sqlite"


def connect(db: pathlib.Path | None = None, readonly: bool = False) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    p = db or path()
    p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if readonly:
        conn = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{p}?mode=ro", uri=True, timeout=30)
        conn.execute("PRAGMA query_only = 1")
    else:
        conn = sqlite3.connect(p, timeout=30, check_same_thread=False)
        conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")
        conn.execute("PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL")
        key = str(p.resolve())
        if key not in _INITED:
            with _LOCK:
                conn.executescript(SCHEMA)
                _INITED.add(key)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    return conn


def _j(x: Any) -> str:
    return json.dumps(x, default=str)


def _safe(fn):
    """Mirroring must never break a run; log and carry on (the file ledger is authoritative, `db sync` catches up)."""
    def wrapper(*a, **kw):
        try:
            return fn(*a, **kw)
        except Exception as e:  # pragma: no cover
            print(f"[preflight.db] {fn.__name__} skipped: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
    wrapper.__name__ = fn.__name__
    return wrapper


# ---- write-through ----
@_safe
def upsert_assessment(assessment_id: str, manifest: dict) -> None:
    with connect() as c:
        c.execute("""INSERT INTO assessments (assessment_id, state, mode, kind, label, target_dir, target_commit, started_at, updated_at,
                     preflight_llm_usd, manifest) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)
                     ON CONFLICT(assessment_id) DO UPDATE SET state=excluded.state, mode=excluded.mode, kind=excluded.kind, label=excluded.label,
                     target_dir=excluded.target_dir, target_commit=excluded.target_commit, started_at=COALESCE(excluded.started_at, assessments.started_at),
                     updated_at=excluded.updated_at, preflight_llm_usd=excluded.preflight_llm_usd, manifest=excluded.manifest""",
                  (assessment_id, manifest.get("state"), manifest.get("mode"), manifest.get("kind", "assessment"), manifest.get("label"),
                   manifest.get("target_dir"), manifest.get("target_commit"), manifest.get("started_at"), time.time(),
                   manifest.get("preflight_llm_usd"), _j(manifest)))


@_safe
def upsert_run(run, steps=None) -> None:
    r = run.model_dump()
    with connect() as c:
        c.execute("""INSERT OR REPLACE INTO runs (run_id, assessment_id, attack_id, seed_id, kind, failed, error, target_commit, mode, started_at,
                     duration_ms, steps, tokens_in, tokens_out, usd, neatlogs_trace_id, neatlogs_url, reply, tool_calls, record)
                     VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)""",
                  (r["run_id"], r["assessment_id"], r["attack_id"], r["seed_id"], r["kind"], int(bool(r["failed"])), r.get("error"),
                   r.get("target_commit"), r.get("mode"), r.get("started_at"), r.get("duration_ms"), r.get("steps"), r.get("tokens_in"),
                   r.get("tokens_out"), r.get("usd"), r.get("neatlogs_trace_id"), r.get("neatlogs_url"), r.get("reply"), _j(r.get("tool_calls")), _j(r)))
        c.execute("DELETE FROM verdicts WHERE run_id = ?", (r["run_id"],))
        c.executemany("INSERT INTO verdicts (run_id, grader, passed, violation_step, evidence) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)",
                      [(r["run_id"], g, int(bool(v["passed"])), v.get("violation_step"), _j(v.get("evidence", []))) for g, v in (r.get("verdicts") or {}).items()])
        if steps is not None:
            c.execute("DELETE FROM steps WHERE run_id = ?", (r["run_id"],))
            c.executemany("INSERT INTO steps (run_id, i, component, type, tool, result_kind, tokens, usd, duration_ms, step) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                          [(r["run_id"], s.i, s.component, s.type, s.tool, s.result_kind, s.tokens, s.usd, s.duration_ms, _j(s.model_dump())) for s in steps])


@_safe
def upsert_cluster(assessment_id: str, cluster) -> None:
    d = cluster.model_dump()
    with connect() as c:
        c.execute("""INSERT OR REPLACE INTO clusters (assessment_id, cluster_id, signature, family, status, attack_ids, run_ids, failing_graders,
                     hypothesis, divergence, record) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)""",
                  (assessment_id, d["cluster_id"], d.get("signature"), d.get("family"), d.get("status"), _j(d.get("attack_ids")), _j(d.get("run_ids")),
                   _j(d.get("failing_graders")), d.get("hypothesis"), _j(d.get("divergence")), _j(d)))


@_safe
def upsert_attempt(assessment_id: str, attempt) -> None:
    d = attempt.model_dump()
    rep = d.get("replay") or {}
    with connect() as c:
        c.execute("""INSERT OR REPLACE INTO attempts (assessment_id, cluster_id, n, author, backend, branch, commit_sha, entire_checkpoint_id, tests_green,
                     status, cost_usd, replay_before, replay_after, summary, record) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)""",
                  (assessment_id, d["cluster_id"], d["n"], d.get("author"), d.get("backend"), d.get("branch"), d.get("commit"), d.get("entire_checkpoint_id"),
                   None if d.get("tests_green") is None else int(bool(d["tests_green"])), d.get("status"), d.get("cost_usd"),
                   rep.get("before") if isinstance(rep, dict) else None, rep.get("after") if isinstance(rep, dict) else None, d.get("summary"), _j(d)))


@_safe
def insert_event(assessment_id: str, ev: dict) -> None:
    with connect() as c:
        c.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO events (assessment_id, seq, ts, type, cluster_id, run_id, payload) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                  (assessment_id, ev.get("seq"), ev.get("ts"), ev.get("type"), ev.get("cluster_id"), ev.get("run_id"), _j(ev)))


@_safe
def upsert_regressions(assessment_id: str, results: Iterable[dict]) -> None:
    with connect() as c:
        for r in results:
            c.execute("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO regressions (assessment_id, cluster_id, passed, blame, record) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)",
                      (assessment_id, r.get("cluster_id"), int(bool(r.get("passed"))), _j(r.get("blame")), _j(r)))


# ---- rebuild from the file ledger ----
def sync_assessment(ledger) -> dict:
    """Rebuild every row of one assessment from its files. Idempotent."""
    from .events import read_events
    upsert_assessment(ledger.assessment_id, ledger.manifest())
    n_runs = 0
    for run in ledger.runs():
        upsert_run(run, ledger.read_steps(run.run_id)); n_runs += 1
    for cl in ledger.clusters():
        upsert_cluster(ledger.assessment_id, cl)
        for a in ledger.attempts(cl.cluster_id):
            upsert_attempt(ledger.assessment_id, a)
    evs = read_events(ledger.root / "events.jsonl")
    with connect() as c:
        c.executemany("INSERT OR REPLACE INTO events (assessment_id, seq, ts, type, cluster_id, run_id, payload) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
                      [(ledger.assessment_id, e.get("seq"), e.get("ts"), e.get("type"), e.get("cluster_id"), e.get("run_id"), _j(e)) for e in evs])
    rep = ledger.root / "report" / "report.json"
    if rep.exists():
        try:
            upsert_regressions(ledger.assessment_id, json.loads(rep.read_text()).get("regressions") or [])
        except Exception:
            pass
    return {"assessment_id": ledger.assessment_id, "runs": n_runs, "events": len(evs)}


def sync_all(base: pathlib.Path | None = None) -> list[dict]:
    from .ledger import Ledger, list_assessments
    return [sync_assessment(Ledger(aid, base=base)) for aid in list_assessments(base)]


# ---- read ----
def query(sql: str, params: tuple = (), limit: int = 500) -> list[dict]:
    """Read-only SQL. Only a single SELECT/WITH statement is accepted; the connection itself is opened read-only."""
    head = sql.lstrip().split(None, 1)[0].upper() if sql.strip() else ""
    if head not in ("SELECT", "WITH", "EXPLAIN") or ";" in sql.rstrip().rstrip(";"):
        raise ValueError("only a single SELECT statement is allowed")
    with connect(readonly=True) as c:
        rows = c.execute(sql, params).fetchmany(limit)
        return [dict(r) for r in rows]


def schema() -> list[dict]:
    with connect(readonly=True) as c:
        return [dict(r) for r in c.execute("SELECT type, name, sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE sql IS NOT NULL ORDER BY type, name")]

"""Preflight CLI."""
from __future__ import annotations
import pathlib
import typer
from rich.console import Console

app = typer.Typer(no_args_is_help=True, help="Preflight crash-tests an AI agent before launch.")
console = Console()

@app.command()
def run(target_dir: pathlib.Path = typer.Argument(..., help="directory containing preflight.yaml"),
        mode: str = typer.Option("dev", help="dev | full"),
        attacks: str = typer.Option(None, help="P0 | D1,E1 | all"),
        seeds: int = typer.Option(None, help="override seeds per attack"),
        label: str = typer.Option(None, help="free-text label stored in the manifest"),
        no_fix: bool = typer.Option(False, "--no-fix", help="stop after clustering (find only)")):
    """Attack, grade, cluster, find divergence, dispatch fixers, replay. Stops at AWAIT_APPROVAL."""
    from .coordinator import Coordinator
    Coordinator(target_dir, mode=mode, attacks=attacks, seeds=seeds, label=label, no_fix=no_fix).run()

@app.command()
def resume(assessment_id: str):
    """Resume an interrupted assessment from its ledger (reuses fixer commits already on the fix branches)."""
    from .coordinator import Coordinator, ensure_proxy
    ensure_proxy()
    Coordinator.from_ledger(assessment_id).resume()

@app.command()
def approve(assessment_id: str, cluster_id: str):
    """Merge the passing fix for a cluster, save it as a regression test; finishes the assessment when all clusters are resolved."""
    from .coordinator import Coordinator
    Coordinator.from_ledger(assessment_id).approve(cluster_id)

@app.command()
def reject(assessment_id: str, cluster_id: str, reason: str = typer.Option(..., "--reason")):
    from .coordinator import Coordinator
    Coordinator.from_ledger(assessment_id).reject(cluster_id, reason)

@app.command("request-changes")
def request_changes(assessment_id: str, cluster_id: str, comment: str = typer.Option(..., "--comment")):
    """Send the reviewer's comment back to the fixer; it revises, then replay runs again."""
    from .coordinator import Coordinator
    Coordinator.from_ledger(assessment_id).request_changes(cluster_id, comment)

@app.command()
def regress(target_dir: pathlib.Path, assessment_id: str = typer.Option(None, help="ledger to record into (default: new)")):
    """Run the saved regression suite against the target's current main."""
    from .coordinator import Coordinator
    from .ledger import new_assessment_id
    c = Coordinator(target_dir, mode="dev", attacks="all", assessment_id=assessment_id or ("regress-" + new_assessment_id()), label="regression-suite")
    from .attacks import catalog as cat
    c.specs = {s.id: s for s in cat.load_all()}
    c.ledger.write_manifest({"assessment_id": c.ledger.assessment_id, "state": "REGRESSION_SUITE", "target_dir": str(c.target_dir), "mode": "dev", "kind": "regress"})
    from .coordinator import ensure_proxy
    ensure_proxy()
    from .llm.gateway import Gateway
    c.gateway = Gateway(on_spend=c._spend)
    res = c.regress(emit=True)
    bad = [r for r in res if not r["passed"]]
    console.print(f"regressions: {len(res)} suites, {len(bad)} regressed")
    raise typer.Exit(code=1 if bad else 0)

@app.command()
def init(target_dir: pathlib.Path):
    """Validate preflight.yaml, check the target is up, verify ownership, discover tools."""
    from .target import loader, manifest, process
    import json
    spec = loader.load(target_dir)
    process.wait_healthy(spec.entry, timeout_s=10)
    process.verify_ownership(spec)
    man = manifest.build(spec)
    console.print_json(json.dumps(man, default=str))

@app.command()
def proxy(port: int = 8300):
    """Run the chaos proxy in the foreground."""
    import uvicorn
    from .chaos.proxy import app as proxy_app
    uvicorn.run(proxy_app, host="0.0.0.0", port=port)

@app.command()
def stop():
    """Kill switch: create the STOP file."""
    from . import config
    (config.ROOT / "STOP").write_text("stop")
    console.print("STOP file written")

@app.command()
def report(assessment_id: str):
    from .ledger import Ledger
    from .report import report as reportmod
    from .attacks import catalog
    led = Ledger(assessment_id)
    specs = {s.id: s for s in catalog.load_all()}
    rep = reportmod.write(led, specs)
    reportmod.print_scorecard(rep["scorecard"], title=assessment_id)

@app.command()
def web(host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: int = 8200):
    """Run the Preflight web API (REST + SSE) for the dashboard."""
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run("preflight.web.app:app", host=host, port=port, log_level="info")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app()

db_app = typer.Typer(no_args_is_help=True, help="SQLite ledger store (ledger/preflight.sqlite, or $PREFLIGHT_DB).")
app.add_typer(db_app, name="db")

@db_app.command("sync")
def db_sync(assessment_id: str = typer.Argument(None, help="one assessment; default: every ledger directory")):
    """Rebuild the SQLite store from the file ledger (idempotent)."""
    from . import db
    from .ledger import Ledger
    out = [db.sync_assessment(Ledger(assessment_id))] if assessment_id else db.sync_all()
    for o in out:
        console.print(f"{o['assessment_id']}: {o['runs']} runs, {o['events']} events")
    console.print(f"store: {db.path()}")

@db_app.command("query")
def db_query(sql: str, as_json: bool = typer.Option(False, "--json")):
    """Run a read-only SELECT against the store."""
    import json as _json
    from rich.table import Table
    from . import db
    try:
        rows = db.query(sql)
    except ValueError as e:
        console.print(f"[red]{e}"); raise typer.Exit(2)
    if as_json:
        print(_json.dumps(rows, indent=2, default=str)); return
    if not rows:
        console.print("(no rows)"); return
    t = Table(*rows[0].keys())
    for r in rows:
        t.add_row(*[str(v)[:80] if v is not None else "" for v in r.values()])
    console.print(t)

@db_app.command("path")
def db_path():
    from . import db
    print(db.path())

@db_app.command("export")
def db_export(dest: pathlib.Path):
    """Copy the store to DEST as one self-contained SQLite file (checkpoints the WAL first)."""
    import shutil
    from . import db
    with db.connect() as c:
        c.execute("PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)")
    shutil.copy(db.path(), dest)
    console.print(f"exported {db.path()} -> {dest} ({dest.stat().st_size // 1024} KB)")

def run(target_dir: pathlib.Path = typer.Argument(..., help="directory containing preflight.yaml"),
        mode: str = typer.Option("dev", help="dev | full"),

        seeds: int = typer.Option(None, help="override seeds per attack"),
        label: str = typer.Option(None, help="free-text label stored in the manifest"),
        no_fix: bool = typer.Option(False, "--no-fix", help="stop after clustering (find only)")):
    """Attack, grade, cluster, find divergence, dispatch fixers, replay. Stops at AWAIT_APPROVAL."""
    from .coordinator import Coordinator
    Coordinator(target_dir, mode=mode, attacks=attacks, seeds=seeds, label=label, no_fix=no_fix).run()

@app.command()
def resume(assessment_id: str):
    """Resume an interrupted assessment from its ledger (reuses fixer commits already on the fix branches)."""
    from .coordinator import Coordinator, ensure_proxy
    ensure_proxy()
    Coordinator.from_ledger(assessment_id).resume()

@app.command()
def approve(assessment_id: str, cluster_id: str):
    """Merge the passing fix for a cluster, save it as a regression test; finishes the assessment when all clusters are resolved."""
    from .coordinator import Coordinator
    Coordinator.from_ledger(assessment_id).approve(cluster_id)

@app.command()
def reject(assessment_id: str, cluster_id: str, reason: str = typer.Option(..., "--reason")):
    from .coordinator import Coordinator
    Coordinator.from_ledger(assessment_id).reject(cluster_id, reason)

@app.command("request-changes")
def request_changes(assessment_id: str, cluster_id: str, comment: str = typer.Option(..., "--comment")):
    """Send the reviewer's comment back to the fixer; it revises, then replay runs again."""
    from .coordinator import Coordinator
    Coordinator.from_ledger(assessment_id).request_changes(cluster_id, comment)

@app.command()
def regress(target_dir: pathlib.Path, assessment_id: str = typer.Option(None, help="ledger to record into (default: new)")):
    """Run the saved regression suite against the target's current main."""
    from .coordinator import Coordinator
    from .ledger import new_assessment_id
    c = Coordinator(target_dir, mode="dev", attacks="all", assessment_id=assessment_id or ("regress-" + new_assessment_id()), label="regression-suite")

    from .coordinator import ensure_proxy
